sources.entry: EME - Open-source Markdown editor with an interface like Chrome. ![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]

summary.one_liner: EME is an open-source desktop Markdown editor with a Chrome-like interface, offering editor/preview toggling, focus mode, export, math typesetting, and optional GitHub Gist sync.
summary.what_it_does: EME is a Markdown editor that lets you show the editor, the preview, or both side by side. It includes a focus mode that hides distractions for writing. The README says it can export Markdown to HTML and PDF, and it supports math typesetting. An optional feature auto-syncs files to a GitHub Gist after they are saved. The README describes the project as a desktop app built with yarn-based build scripts that produce .dmg, .exe, and .deb binaries.
use_cases: Writing Markdown documents in a distraction-free environment
Exporting Markdown to HTML or PDF
Backing up Markdown files to a GitHub Gist
how_to_run: Download the latest release from the Releases link in the README
yarn win # builds .exe, yarn linux # builds .deb
stack: Electron (implied by build targets, not named in README)
notable: Chrome-like tabbed interface for editor and preview
Optional auto-sync of saved files to GitHub Gist
caveats: The README has a WIKI section that is only a placeholder with no content
Contribution steps depend on yarn and a watch-and-start workflow; no platform requirements are listed beyond the build targets
